title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Japamala direction. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Japamala
options.lineage: The japamala of namasmarana: 108 beads and the guru bead, counted one by one
options.thesis: The session is a mala: each bhajan is one bead, and its words arrive strung on a thread.
options.viewport: One guru bead, centred on a dark rudraksha ground, is the Start button; when the bhajan is found its letters are strung in along a vermilion thread and the bead slides down the cord to rest below the lyrics.
options.risk: Beads can drift into decoration; the bead must stay obviously a button, and projector legibility beats any thread effect.

options.label: Still line on a drifting void
options.thesis: Lyrics as dead-still ivory lines on a black void while grey dust drifts behind; an amber caret is the listening state.
options.case: Calm and readable on a projector, but demoscene is foreign to a Sai hall and it sits close to the karaoke-black rut.

options.label: Step-row listener
options.thesis: Listening is a lit step row chasing through the 3, 5, 7, 9 and 10-second checks before the words land.
options.case: Makes the wait legible, but a rhythm-machine panel fights the devotional mood and adds nothing to the lyrics screen itself.

options.label: Wood-type broadside
options.thesis: Every lyric line set as a full-width wood-type band, stamped onto the screen one press-pull per line.
options.case: The strongest legibility from the back of a hall; a gig-poster voice is a stretch for devotional singing.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark lyric screen: white centred text, a simple fade between bhajans, a plain round button.
canonCard.viewport: Black screen, centred white sans-serif lyrics filling the frame, a pill-shaped button below.
